identity.title: Revela: Dense Retriever Learning via Language Modeling

problem.claim: The paper asks how language-model-style self-supervised objectives can train dense retrievers without relying on costly, scarce annotated query-document pairs.

contributions.claim: Introduces Revela, a unified and scalable framework that trains retrievers through language modeling over local and cross-document context.
Uses retriever-weighted in-batch attention so similarity computation participates in next-token-prediction training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present Revela as a unified framework for self-supervised retriever learning via language modeling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, without annotated or synthetic query-document pairs, Revela surpasses larger supervised models and proprietary APIs on CoIR and BRIGHT.
The authors report achieving BEIR's unsupervised state of the art with approximately 1000× less training data and 10× less compute.
The authors report that performance increases with batch size and model size across their evaluation, which they interpret as evidence of scalability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dense retrievers support access to external knowledge, but annotated training pairs are costly and scarce in specialized or reasoning-intensive settings.
The paper connects next-token prediction with learning dependencies among token chunks and asks how to adapt this idea to retriever training.
Revela learns document dependencies by conditioning next-token prediction on local and cross-document context through retriever-weighted in-batch attention.
Across domain-specific, reasoning-intensive, and general-domain benchmarks, the authors report strong comparisons, data/compute efficiency, and scaling with batch and model size.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links the proposed retriever objective to next-token prediction and specifies how similarity-weighted attention implements that link.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete analogy can make a new objective easier to motivate when the mechanism translating the analogy is also stated.
lessons.application: When introducing a self-supervised objective, pair the motivating learning principle with the exact conditioning, weighting, or optimization mechanism that operationalizes it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the analogy does not yield a well-defined training mechanism or when the target task lacks a meaningful dependency structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark scores, statistical details, baseline identities, or the exact training-data and compute accounting behind the reported comparisons.
It does not specify which retriever backbones, batch sizes, model sizes, or data subsets produced the reported scaling and efficiency results.
